title: Crafting a Team Charter to Work Through the Storming Phase
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Drawing on Bruce Tuckman's classic stages of group development, this article focuses on the Storming phase, when early cordiality gives way to friction and more candid disagreement. The author recommends that team leaders respond by building a formal Team Charter rather than letting conflict fester unaddressed. The charter should spell out team purpose, goals, roles, and especially specific behavioral norms, since concrete rules of conduct do more to reduce friction than vague principles. Once drafted, the charter works best when team members publicly commit to it and agree to hold each other accountable to it. The piece frames the charter not as a way to avoid conflict but as a structure that lets a team move through conflict productively toward stronger collaboration.
points: Tuckman's five stages of group development include a Storming phase marked by rising candor and conflict
A Team Charter combines purpose, goals, roles, and specific behavioral norms
Specific behavioral rules ('wait for our turn to speak') outperform general principles ('be respectful')
Public commitment to the charter creates mutual accountability among team members
Successful teams don't avoid conflict during Storming, they work through it with structure
quotes: During the Storming stage, team members settle in, get more comfortable with each other, and become more candid in their discussions.
How a team handles and works through the Storming stage is critically important for long-term success.

A Team Charter is a collaboratively produced agreement that commonly includes four critical components: a succinctly stated Team purpose, a list of long-term Team goals and objectives, Team roles and responsibilities, and a catalog of Team norms and ground rules.
The rules describe the specific behaviors the team agrees to abide by.
Once the charter exists, the team leader should ask everyone on the team to publicly commit to the standards and agree to confront any violation of the agreed-upon rules of engagement.
Successful team collaboration is not the absence of conflict but the ability to work through it.
